//: AION SoC - LibreLane configuration template.
This file is never handed to LibreLane directly. scripts/prepare_librelane_config.py
resolves the source list from FuseSoC, rewrites paths relative to the run
directory, applies the '_modes' overlay for the requested target and writes
the result to <run dir>/config.json. The '//' and '_modes' keys are stripped
on the way out.
Targets:  make synth | make pnr | make pnr_simple
TinyTapeout compatibility
Both PnR targets harden the chip as the tile itself: the GDS TT receives is
the one this flow writes, byte for byte, through tt-gds-action/custom_gds.
That action routes nothing -- it copies the GDS, LEF and netlist and runs
the precheck on them -- and the precheck demands the tile's exact die area
and the template DEF's exact pin rectangles. So a smaller macro is not
something TT can wire up; the tile has to be built here. The keys below
are the ones tt-support-tools' create_user_config() and TT's
src/config.json set for an ihp-sg13g2 project, less the ones that only buy
CI time (RUN_KLAYOUT_XOR, RUN_KLAYOUT_DRC) or are tuning TT leaves to the
user. `make tt_precheck` runs TT's own precheck on the result.
https://github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-support-tools/blob/main/project.py
https://github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-support-tools/blob/main/precheck/precheck.py
https://github.com/TinyTapeout/ttihp-verilog-template/blob/main/src/config.json
The *_VIOLATION_CORNERS lists are pinned rather than left to their
defaults. Setup and hold already covered every corner (setup via the
TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS fallback, hold via its own default), but max
slew and max cap default to [""], which LibreLane filters down to an
empty corner list -- so those two checkers examined nothing and still
reported 'No ... violations found'. The 'lenient' overlay empties all five.
//floorplan: DIE_AREA is tile_sizes.yaml's entry for a 4x2 ihp-sg13g2 tile, and has to
equal the DIEAREA of the DEF template the Makefile passes
the 43 pins, on Metal4 along the north edge, and the precheck compares
both the LEF SIZE and every pin rectangle against it.
scripts/prepare_librelane_config.py refuses a run where the two disagree.
There is no CORE_AREA. The margins below put the rows exactly where the
template's ROW statements have them -- one row from the top and bottom
edges, six sites from the sides -- and they are not cosmetic: the PDN
stripes end where the core does (3.15 um from the bottom edge and 3.56 um
from the top, as built), and the precheck wants every power stripe within
10 um of both. LibreLane's default of four rows would end them ~15 um in.
//power: The precheck wants VPWR and VGND as LEF pins on TopMetal1, at least
2.1 um wide, spanning the tile top to bottom -- the harness drops its own
TopMetal2 straps across them. PDN_MULTILAYER off keeps the grid to those
vertical TopMetal1 stripes (PDN_HORIZONTAL_LAYER is TopMetal2 for this
PDK, a layer the precheck forbids outright), and MAGIC_WRITE_LEF_PINONLY
keeps the rails and vias out of the pin ports, where the precheck would
read them as power pins on the wrong layer. MAGIC_DEF_LABELS off is TT's
workaround for an LVS problem; PDN_VPITCH is TT's stripe pitch.
//routing: RT_MAX_LAYER is tech.py's project_top_metal_layer for ihp-sg13g2: routing
stops at TopMetal1. The PDK default is TopMetal2, which the precheck
rejects. Output ports are left unbuffered, as TT's own flow leaves them.
//antenna: RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION stays off, LibreLane's default. The heuristic
puts an sg13g2_antennanp (5.44 um2) on every pin of every net whose pins span
90 um or more -- drivers included, and whether or not the net violates
anything. Measured on this design: 4860 diodes on pnr_simple and 5141 on the
AION netlist (~26,000-28,000 um2, a quarter of the logic), against 1 and 2
violations that OpenROAD.RepairAntennas (on by default) then fixes with 1
diode or with jumpers -- 0 antenna violations after detailed routing on both.
Check route__antenna_violation__count after a run before turning it back on.

//: Overlays merged on top of the base configuration by
scripts/prepare_librelane_config.py. 'lenient' is applied last and is
enabled with LENIENT=1 on any make target.
CELL_LIBS -- the standard-cell Liberty the technology mapper reads --
is NOT set here. `make synth` passes --cell-lib to
scripts/prepare_librelane_config.py, one per STA corner, pointing at
the extended library scripts/merge_lib.py builds from the PDK's cells
plus the hand-designed ones under implementation/pdk_extension/. It
has to be a path relative to the run directory, which only that
script knows. PDK_EXT=0 leaves the PDK library in place.
`make pnr_simple` never gets the flag: it is the PDK-only baseline.
PnR from a pre-existing netlist that may instantiate AI-generated cells.
RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_RX is deliberately left at its default ('$^', matches
nothing). Setting it to '^_AION_.*' marks every AI cell instance
don't-touch, and OpenROAD then refuses to insert a fanout buffer in
front of ANY of their input pins -- repair_design aborts with
RSZ-3006 on the first high-fanout net that feeds one. 46 of the
netlist's 65 nets with fanout > MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT drive an AI
cell, so this is not a net the flow can route around.
The cells do not need the protection: their liberty functions are
4-input fusions with no equivalent in sg13g2, so the resizer has
nothing to swap them for, they are neither buffers nor inverters, and
DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS is false. Confirm they survived by
grepping the hardened netlist -- flow/7_pnr/nl/tt_um_aion.nl.v --
for the AION_ masters after a run.
Downgrade every hard checker so a broken custom cell still yields a
GDS and a full set of reports to look at. Never use for signoff.
